info.name: ITSthe1.ID API v1.0.0
info.description:
# ITSthe1.ID API - complete request collection

Every endpoint this build serves, with a ready-to-send payload for each of the business transactions. Generated from `docs/payloads/*.json`; the companion reference is `docs/PAYLOADS.md` and the handover report is `docs/PARTNER_HANDOVER.md`.

## Set up

1. Import this file **and** `ITSthe1.ID.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select the *ITSthe1.ID - local* environment and set `baseUrl` to the host running the API (default `http://localhost:5030`).
3. Run **1. Monitoring -> GET /health** first. If it is not `healthy: true`, stop and fix the environment before anything else.

## How the variables flow

You should not have to paste ids by hand. Test scripts capture them:

| Variable | Set by | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `checkinUID` | any `POST /checkin` | everything downstream |
| `guestUID` | `POST /guest`, `GET /guest` | attachment, guest check-out |
| `mainGuestUID` | `GET /guest` | main-guest handover (the departing guest) |
| `newMainGuestUID` | `POST /guest`, `GET /guest` | main-guest handover (the successor) |

## Three things that will cost you an afternoon

- **`GET /checkin` and `GET /guest` take a JSON body.** Postman handles it; PowerShell 5.1 cannot send a body on a GET at all.
- **`uid` means two different things.** `POST /checkin` returns *checkinguest* ids; `POST /guest` and `GET /guest` return *guest* ids. Every other endpoint wants the guest id. Always take ids from `GET /guest`.
- **A 200 from a lookup can still be a failure.** Those handlers catch their own database errors and answer 200 with `{"error": "..."}`. The tests in folders 2 and 3 assert on the body for this reason.

## Order that works

Monitoring -> lookups -> `POST /checkin` (cash) -> `GET /checkin` -> `POST /guest` (escort) -> `GET /guest` -> `POST /guestattachment` -> `POST /roomchange` -> `POST /guestcheckout` -> `POST /checkout`.

Timestamps in the payloads are already ordered for this sequence. If you edit them, keep: check-in < escort check-in < room change < escort check-out < check-out.

item.name: 4. Check-in
item.description:
`POST /checkin` is the entry point for every other transaction - it is the only thing that mints a `CheckinUID`.

The **Run the collection** order that works: *POST cash* -> *GET /checkin* -> the escort folder -> departure. The POST captures `checkinUID` into a collection variable automatically, so the later requests need no editing.

request.description:
**This GET carries a JSON body.** Postman and `curl.exe` can do it; PowerShell 5.1's `Invoke-RestMethod` refuses outright (*Cannot send a content-body with this verb-type*).

Defaults to `CheckinUID: 6`, an open stay in the reference database. Change it to `{{checkinUID}}` to read back the stay you just created.

Unknown id -> **404** `Check-in not found`.

The simplest valid check-in: one main guest, cash, room `003`.

Creates payment -> check-in -> guest -> document -> checkinguest -> log -> guestversion, then flags the room. **Not transactional** - a failure part way through leaves orphan rows behind.

Change `RoomNumber` to a room that is free (`GET /room`, `IsChecked = false`).

`IsHouseUse` **must be present and false** - the guard reads `data.get('IsHouseUse', True)`, so omitting the key is read as *house use* and the cash payment is rejected with 40035.

request.description:
The identifier is **`UID`**, not `CheckinUID` - the only endpoint that differs.

`Guests[]` must carry the *full* guest objects (not a delta), exactly one `IsMainGuest: true`, and every `CheckoutDateTime` must stay `null` (40023). 40011 if the stay is already checked out.

**Known defect:** the handler finds the row to update by the guest's newest `checkinguest` row across *every* check-in, so a repeat visitor on a newer stay gets the wrong row edited. Keep test guests unique per stay.

item.name: 5. Guests and escorts
item.description:
"Escort" is this API's word for anyone on the stay who is not the main guest.

**Two ways to add one:** inside `Guests[]` at check-in (folder 4), or `POST /guest` afterwards - the *add escort* button in the desktop client. This folder is the second path.

**`EscortTypeId` is hard-coded to 2 (AdultEscort)** in all three write paths. There is no payload field for it, so `ChildEscort` is never written and `AdultEscortCount` / `ChildEscortCount` stay `null` on every check-in row. `GET /escorttype` still serves both values for the dropdown.

**Escort timestamps gate everything downstream.** Room change and check-out are both compared against the newest `checkinguest` row, so order your test timestamps: check-in < escort check-in < room change < escort check-out < check-out.

request.description:
**Body on a GET again.** Lists every guest on a stay.

**Run this after any write** - it is the only reliable source of *guest ids*, which `POST /guestattachment`, `POST /guestcheckout` and `NewMainGuestUID` all require. The `uid` returned by `POST /checkin` is a *checkinguest* id and will silently address the wrong record.

The tests on this request capture `mainGuestUID` and `guestUID` for you.

exec: pm.test('at least one guest on the stay', () => pm.expect(gs.length).to.be.above(0));
const main = gs.find(g => g.IsMainGuest === true || g.isMainGuest === true);
const escort = gs.find(g => !(g.IsMainGuest === true || g.isMainGuest === true));

item.name: 6. Attachments
item.description:
Guest documents. Base64 JPEG, **under 200 KB decoded** (60004). Every payload in this collection carries the same valid 1x1 JPEG so nothing depends on a local file.

Images are resized to 1080x720 and re-encoded at quality 85, written under `BaseDirectoryPath` on the API host **and** stored as a blob in the database - so these endpoints touch the filesystem as well as SQL Server.

request.description:
Extra documents for a guest already on an open stay.

`GuestUID` is the **guest id** from `GET /guest`, not the checkinguest id.

Codes: 40009, 40010, 40011, 50010 (no `GuestUID`), 60001 (no attachments), 60004 (over 200 KB).

Unlike the other write endpoints this one **de-duplicates filenames**: a second `Image_2.jpg` is stored as `Image_2_1.jpg`. On `POST /checkin` and `POST /guest` there is no such rename, so a guest's second document needs a distinct `Name`.
Attachment metadata rows.

**Currently fails on the reference database** - returns HTTP 200 with an `{"error": "42S02 Invalid object name ...guestdocumentimages"}` body. See the known-issues section of the handover report; the `CREATE TABLE` is supplied there.

item.name: 7. Departure and handover
item.description:
Three different ways a stay ends: one guest leaves, everyone leaves, or the whole check-in is cancelled.

All three enforce the same ordering rule - the timestamp must be after every guest's check-in, after any room change, after any main-guest change, and after the newest escort's check-in **and** check-out.

request.description:
One guest departs; the stay continues.

`GuestUID` is a **guest id**. Rules: stay open (40011), `CheckoutDateTime` present (40014), not before that guest's check-in (40032), not in the future (40004), guest not already checked out (50017).

The main guest leaves and an escort takes over the stay. Driven **entirely** by `NewMainGuestUID` - there is no separate main-guest-change endpoint (`GET /mainguestchange` is a read-only dump).

In order, the API: writes a `MainGuestChange` row and a log entry; clears `IsMainGuest` on the outgoing guest and copies the incoming guest's relationship onto them; sets `IsMainGuest` on the successor and clears their relationship; snapshots a new `guestversion`; and only then checks the departing guest out.

**Always name a successor.** If the main guest leaves without one, this build does not reject the request - it checks them out and leaves the stay with no main guest, which breaks later `guestversion` writes.

Closes the stay, frees the room, stamps `CheckoutDate` on every guest still in it, writes a `checkout` row with `CheckoutTypeId = 1`.

40010 if cancelled, 40011 if already checked out, 40034 if before a guest's dates, 40004 if in the future, 40039 if a house-use stay asks for a late check-out.

Returns a **bare** `{"CheckinUID": n}` - not the envelope. Only its errors use the envelope.

  "CheckinUID": "{{checkinUID}}",
  "IsLateCheckout": false,
  "CheckoutDateTime": "2026-08-04T10:30:00",
  "Comment": "payload collection - close the stay",

  "ClientUID": "Establishment101",
  "MessageUID": null,
  "CorrelationUID": "test-checkout-001",
  "Timestamp": "2026-08-04T10:30:00"
}

request.description: Adjusts a check-out that has already happened. Requires the stay to be **inactive** - 40031 if it is still active, the mirror image of the POST. Same date rules, code 40032.

Cancels a check-in rather than closing it: writes a `checkout` row with `CheckoutTypeId = 2` and a reason, frees the room, closes out every guest.

`CancellationReasonCode` is `Unhappy` or `UserError`. 40011 if already checked out, 40010 if already cancelled, 40025 if the cancellation predates the check-in, 40004 if in the future - plus a free-text refusal if the current month is later than the check-in's month.

**Run this only on a check-in you created for the test.** Returns a bare `{"CheckinUID": n}`.

The date field is **`EffectiveDate`**, not `EffectiveDateTime`.

`NewRoomNumber` must exist (80001) and be free (80003). `EffectiveDate` must not be in the future, and must be after the stay's check-in, after any previous room change, after any main-guest change, and after the newest escort's check-in and check-out.
